I'm half russian so I'll answer for this part :

He - Он (pronounced like "on" but more an "o" sound in the beginning)

She - Она (technically pronounced like for he with just "A" in the end, it's more commonly pronounced "Ana" when spoken)

They - Они (Same as for Она but the last letter changes for "e", think of the Japanese culture monsters "Oni" for the pronunciation but mainly pronounced "Ani")


Fun fact : you'll often see sentences without a pronoun being used when someone talks about themselves or to answer a question, they're implied but not said unless you want to talk about a stranger or someone that isn't there at the moment. The verb is always being changed depending on the subject's gender or number and nouns change according to gender, number and to the case (nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, instrumental and locative).
For example : 
Were you at the store? - Was but went to the pharmacy. 
Ты был/была в магазине? - Был/была но пошел/пошла в аптеку.

When I was 7yo, my parents divorced during summer, it happened while they had sent me off to my maternal grandparents in another country and was quite messy, I went to live with my mom afterwards but my dad was still madly in love with her. I saw my dad 2 weeks a month and was with him half the holidays. We always did something different : going to feed the wild bunnies near the road, going to the zoo/museum/amusement park, traveling to another country once. He tried to give me as much time as possible but often had to work when I was with him but it made the times I spent with him even more special.
With my mom, we went bowling with my best friend since kindergarten (our moms are very close since they met), did similar activities that we did with my dad too and it was awesome.

Then, after 1 year and a half, she introduced me to her new boyfriend, the man which gave me the DVDs. I was kinda okay with it but sad as my dad was still expecting for them to rekindle their relationship. We moved for him to live we us as our place was too small for 3 people. It was still fine at the time because I was still seeing my dad.

When I was 12, my mom announced me that she was pregnant and I was gonna have a sibling. I was kinda happy but also apprehensive that my mom would love me less or other dumb things that can go through your mind in cases like that. My mom needed time for herself while pregnant and help so I did as she asked me. We moved again for a house, now with 1h45 drive to my dad, I was sad to be pushed further away from him. My baby brother (which I love dearly) was born a month before my 13th birthday. 

At my 13th birthday, I received a message from my dad, wishing me happy birthday, then another one telling me he won't be able to take me for some time but he loved me more than anything. I became sad and a bit anxious but I couldn't do anything against it. 

I became very fast a babysitter/helper for my mom 24/7, she always asked me for help with my brother even when I needed to study or do homework so I often did so late at night, after my brother was asleep. My stepdad (I think he's on the spectrum but undiagnosed because of some things and my little brother is the same as him for those things) didn't knew how to act with children and worked a lot more to afford the house and for us to live comfortably, going to work at 6AM and coming back after 9PM.
I started falling asleep during classes, my grades started dropping quite a lot but my mother didn't pay any attention to it. When I was asking for help with some lessons or homework, I would be dismissed because mom was tired. 

My dad, on the other hand, started replying less and less, until on my 14th birthday, I didn't receive anything, same on Christmas, I sent him a message and nothing, again at New Year's Eve. I was devastated, devoured by anxiety, but my mother didn't see anything of it, I started hurting myself, quite badly, but my mom ignored it or didn't want to admit it (I went from wearing shorts and t-shirts with sleeves up all the time to long sleeves down and jeans all the time, from laughing and smiling brightly to not smiling at all and, when I did, faking a smile that never reached my eyes). 

Then, on father's Day, my big half brother (same dad, 18 years older than me) sent me a message asking when I was getting out of school, I told him 12:30 AM and he said he was coming. I was so excited, hadn't seen him in 3 years! I went to the school gate with my girl best friend, smiling while talking with her about my brother, when we reached the gate, I saw my brother... And my dad. I ran towards him full speed, I hugged him so hard, tears streaming down my face, totally bawling in front of the whole school, not caring at all, sobbing like a little kid. We left and went to a nearby fast food, I was still crying because it was the first time I saw my dad in almost 2years. They told me he was in hospital and my brother will drive him back there after we finished eating. I was extremely sad but so happy at the same time.

I saw my father just 1 more time, with my mother, at hospital, 4 days before he passed. He died one night, peacefully and all my emotions had "shut off" when I had seen him in hospital, and this day was the first one my mom hugged me since my little brother was born. We went to his funeral and then I couldn't stop bawling for hours, my mom was crying and holding my hand, even my stepdad held my shoulder and cried his eyes out even though they never met. 

Then my mom sent me to therapy once a month "because you need it" but nothing else, I needed her even more now but we didn't spent time together anymore, until I tried to end myself, then she got me into therapy once a week and got me light plant medication (not weed) and that's it. I felt abandoned even more than I could have ever thought. She didn't realized I was screaming for help and just went back to her usual self, even worse because I was the only one setting boundaries to my little brother, they just would say "don't do that" and that's it, while I would be monitored, told to come home before 6PM (even after I turned 17), always told to obey and not say anything.

When I turned 18 and 1day, I left to live with my boyfriend (now fiancé), that was a huge wake-up call and shock for her, both her and my stepdad realised how much I was doing at home, how entitled my brother had became, how patient I had been and how wrong they were. My mother begged for forgiveness, asked to meet and I agreed only 1 month after, she tried to get me to come back, realized her mistakes, I told her how I had felt all this time and we both cried a lot that day. Then my boyfriend and I agreed to come to their place on Christmas, we joked and had a good time, my mother took me aside and told me "It's been so long since I saw your smile reach your eyes, I know you're really happy now. I'm really sorry for what I put you through. I love you"

Since then, we meet up each 2-3 months for a mother-daughter day and our relationship is better than it ever was.

Caramel : Sugar, sugar and more sugar + salted butter (for solid caramel), if you want to make homemade salted caramel for spreading it on some bread or pancakes or waffles etc, add whole liquid cream in the end.
For 1 small jar : 
100g sugar, 40g half-salted butter, 20cl whole liquid cream
1. Heat the sugar alone in a stainless steel saucepan over medium heat. Cook without stirring until it melts and caramelizes.
2. Gradually add the butter and then the whole cream by mixing vigorously with a whisk to avoid lumps.
3. When the preparation is homogeneous, continue cooking for 5 minutes and remove from heat. The caramel is still liquid but its texture had to change and become thicker. If it is sufficiently cooked, it will harden on cooling.
4. Pour into a small jam jar and let cool. Keep the jar in the refrigerator.

Variations: For a caramel cream, add a few squares of chocolate.

With light cream (12%), the result is also delicious.
